content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm looking to find out if it's possible to set up communication between a Data Logic DS2400n-0210 barcode scanner and a [product_name] PLC from [company_name]. The issue I'm facing is that the barcode scanner I have only supports RS232 and RS485 interfaces, not Ethernet. Is there a way to connect it to a [product_name] PLC?

[product_name] versions [article_no] and [article_no] only support Ethernet TCP/IP with S7 protocol. Newer models, such as [product_name] [article_no] or above, can use Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol and also support Modbus TCP/IP.

Thanks for the reply. If I use an RS232-to-Ethernet converter, is it possible then to establish communication between these two devices? Also, is there any sample software or program to use as an example?

I'm not sure which protocol the scanner uses. The [product_name] PLC only supports the S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP. A converter will only change the physical connection type, not the protocol itself. I can confirm only what the [product_name] PLC supports and am not certain about the scanner's capabilities. You should contact the scanner's manufacturer for more details.

analysis.insight_summary: Users tried to connect a Data Logic barcode scanner with RS232/RS485 interface to a [product_name] PLC from [company_name]. They found that the PLC only supports Ethernet TCP/IP via S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP on newer models. The core challenge was that physical converters do not address the protocol compatibility gap between the devices. Users were unsure how to bridge this gap or obtain a solution for protocol conversion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to communicate between the barcode scanner and [company_name] PLC using the available interfaces, possibly by adding a hardware converter and finding example software for reference.
